statement: Sketch the graph of $y=|x^{2}-4|$ and solve $|x^{2}-4|=3$.
solution:
The graph of $y=x^{2}-4$ is a parabola crossing the $x$-axis at $x=\pm2$. Reflecting the part below the $x$-axis gives the graph of $y=|x^{2}-4|$.
To solve $|x^{2}-4|=3$ we consider two cases:
$$x^{2}-4=3\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^{2}=7\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=\pm\sqrt7,$$
$$x^{2}-4=-3\quad\Rightarrow\quad x^{2}=1\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=\pm1.$$
So $x=\pm1,\pm\sqrt7$.
hints: Start from the parabola y = x^2 - 4.
Reflect any negative part above the axis.
